messages:
maria: Heads up — onboarding Llama-3-8B-q4f16. After converting an HF chat_template to Redwood prompt format we see duplicated assistant prefixes and replies getting truncated ~120 tokens in our eval suite. Minimal repro below, anyone seen this?

suman: Can you paste the HF template snippet you converted? dynamic role stuff often trips the converter.

maria: Sure, simplified version — template uses a macro + role variable:

```jinja
{% macro render_msg(m) -%}
{{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}
{%- endmacro %}

{% for h in history -%}
{{ render_msg(h) }}
{%- endfor %}
```

And incoming history objects look like: `{"role": "{{speaker_role}}", "content": "{{utterance}}"}` (the role is a runtime expression in our pipeline).

kai: Ah — that pattern will produce literal `{{speaker_role}}` in the intermediate text if you run the HF-to-Redwood converter before the Jinja is fully rendered. Redwood's converter expects concrete role names (system/user/assistant) to map them to the correct sentinels. If it sees `{{...}}` it treats it as text and inserts role-sentinels incorrectly.

jeff: That would explain duplicated prefixes — converter sees `{{speaker_role}}: ...` and wraps it like `<|role_{{speaker_role}}|>...` which confuses the tokenizer and leads to truncated outputs during decoding. Did you see any special-tokens in the tokenization logs?

maria: Yes, tokenizer logs show unexpected tokens around the start of assistant blocks, e.g.:

```
... tokens: [50256, 50257, 12, 345, ...]
mapping: <|role_{{speaker_role}}|> -> [50256,50257]
```

and the eval harness flags a shift in token distribution exactly where the literal role placeholder appears.

suman: Two quick fixes to try: 1) pre-render the Jinja (so roles are concrete) before running HF->Redwood conversion; 2) add a converter pass that recognizes common Jinja var patterns and rejects or expands them. Which is easier for your pipeline?

maria: We tried pre-rendering in CI for the failing tests and it fixed the duplication/truncation locally. But we have many templates that intentionally delay rendering (per-customer role injection) so pre-rendering isn't always possible.

kai: Another option: add a config.json mapping stage that lists role_aliases and fallback heuristics. Example: `"chat_template": { "role_aliases": { "assistant": ["assistant","bot","agent"], "user": ["user","customer"] } }` — but that still requires the role token to be literal. It won't help if there are raw `{{...}}` tokens at conversion time.

jeff: Could we update the converter to detect `{{`/`}}` and emit a warning+placeholder token that our tokenizer knows to strip (e.g., `<|redwood:jinja_var|>`)? Then downstream renders can substitute real roles before final encode. That might preserve templates while avoiding accidental special token creation.

oncall-bot: quick ci run report — job 4821: template-pre-render tests: 14/15 passed, failing case = dynamic-role-path. Full logs: https://ci.internal/runs/4821 (private).

maria: Sounds good. I'll open a small RFC/PR: two parts — (A) a converter guard that detects unrendered Jinja expressions in role positions and either errors or inserts a neutral placeholder; (B) add tooling to our onboarding script to optionally pre-render only the role fields (not content) when safe.

suman: +1. Also add a regression eval into the model onboarding checklist: token-distribution diff and a sanity check that assistant prefixes are not duplicated. We saw similar issues mask as quantization regressions earlier.

maria: Agreed. I'll include a short reproducer and the tokenizer dump in the PR. For now work-around: pre-render roles in the failing customer's template and re-run the q4f16 evals. Thanks all :pray:

kai: Nice find. If anyone else hits this, ping me and I can help instrument the converter to detect `{{...}}` in role slots. :thinking:
